tr.en: As population ageing deepens, China's population aged sixty and over has passed three hundred million. This huge group means pressure on pensions and health care, but it also holds enormous spending potential. In recent years the "silver economy" built around older people's needs has been becoming a new engine of growth. Contrary to the stereotype, today's older people aren't content with merely being fed and clothed. Many are well educated, had stable incomes before retiring and have built up some wealth, and their attitudes to spending are ever more open: more and more older consumers appear in travel, fitness, culture and entertainment, and online learning. A survey shows some people born in the 1960s spend more per head on travel than some younger groups. Yet supply hasn't kept up. On one hand, products suited to older people are limited, and many ignore their physical traits and habits; on the other, false advertising and health-supplement scams aimed at the elderly persist despite bans, damaging their trust. Insiders say the key is truly understanding older people: companies should move from "making products for the elderly" to "making products with them", inviting older users to help design and test, while regulators should crack down harder on fraud targeting the elderly and create a consumer environment where they can feel safe.

items.text:
随着人口老龄化程度不断加深，中国六十岁及以上人口已超过三亿。这一庞大的群体不仅意味着养老、医疗等方面的压力，也孕育着巨大的消费潜力。近年来，围绕老年人需求而形成的“银发经济”，正逐渐成为拉动经济增长的新引擎。
与人们的刻板印象不同，如今的老年人并不满足于“吃饱穿暖”。他们中的许多人受过良好教育，退休前收入稳定，积累了一定的财富，消费观念也日趋开放。旅游、健身、文化娱乐、在线学习等领域，都出现了越来越多老年消费者的身影。有调查显示，部分“六十后”在旅游上的人均花费，甚至超过了一些年轻群体。
然而，市场的供给却未能完全跟上。一方面，适合老年人的产品种类有限，不少商品在设计上忽视了老年人的身体特点和使用习惯；另一方面，针对老年人的虚假宣传、保健品骗局屡禁不止，损害了老年消费者的信任。
业内人士指出，发展银发经济，关键在于真正读懂老年人。企业需要从“为老年人做产品”转向“和老年人一起做产品”，邀请老年用户参与设计和测试；监管部门则应加大对涉老诈骗的打击力度，为老年人营造安心、放心的消费环境。

tr.en: Mention the brain and people think first of the complex organ in the head. But more and more research shows our gut holds a "second brain". About five hundred million nerve cells line the gut wall — as many as in a cat's brain. This vast nervous system can run independently of the brain, controlling digestion on its own. More surprisingly, gut and brain keep up a frequent "conversation" through nerves and hormones, each influencing the other. Scientists have found trillions of microbes living in the gut, forming the "gut flora". They not only help break down food and make certain vitamins but produce substances that affect mood: most of the body's serotonin — closely tied to feelings of pleasure — is made in the gut. Research finds people with unbalanced gut flora are more prone to anxiety and depression. These findings open new approaches to treating some mental illnesses. But researchers caution that the gut–mood link is very complex; most studies are still at the animal-experiment stage, far from clinical use. Rather than putting blind faith in supplements claiming to "regulate the gut", a balanced diet and regular routine are the most reliable way to keep the gut healthy.

提到大脑，人们首先想到的是头部那个复杂的器官。然而，越来越多的研究表明，我们的肠道里也存在着一个“第二大脑”。
人的肠道壁上分布着大约五亿个神经细胞，数量与猫的大脑相当。这套庞大的神经系统可以独立于大脑运作，自主控制消化过程。更令人惊讶的是，肠道与大脑之间通过神经和激素保持着频繁的“对话”，彼此影响。
科学家发现，肠道中生活着数以万亿计的微生物，它们构成了“肠道菌群”。这些微生物不仅帮助人体分解食物、合成某些维生素，还能产生影响情绪的物质。人体内大部分的血清素——一种与愉悦感密切相关的物质——就是在肠道中产生的。有研究发现，肠道菌群失衡的人，更容易出现焦虑、抑郁等情绪问题。
这些发现为治疗某些心理疾病提供了新思路。不过，研究人员也提醒，肠道与情绪之间的关系十分复杂，目前大多数研究仍停留在动物实验阶段，距离真正应用于临床还有很长的路要走。与其迷信各种号称能“调理肠道”的保健品，不如保持均衡饮食、规律作息，这才是维护肠道健康最可靠的方式。

tr.en: A "Survey Report on Young People's Reading" just released by a research institute shows that of the five thousand 18-to-35-year-olds surveyed, 82 per cent said they had read at least one book in the past year — nine points more than five years ago. Meanwhile the way they read has changed markedly: for the first time e-reading (56 per cent) has overtaken print, and users of "listening to books" — taking in a book's content as audio — are growing fast, nearly thirty per cent. The report notes young readers' reading time is clearly "fragmented": over sixty per cent read mainly in scattered moments — commuting, lunch breaks, before sleep — for under half an hour at a time. Literature and psychology are the most popular, followed by history and economics and management. Notably, although more people read, the share of "deep reading" is falling: fewer than twenty per cent had finished a book of over three hundred pages in the past year. Researchers believe the rise of short videos and similar entertainment makes it ever harder for young people to concentrate for long. The report suggests libraries, bookshops and the like organise reading groups and courses in deep reading to help the young form the habit of systematic reading.

某研究机构近日发布的《青年阅读状况调查报告》显示，在受访的五千名十八至三十五岁青年中，有百分之八十二的人表示过去一年读过至少一本书，比五年前提高了九个百分点。与此同时，阅读方式发生了显著变化：选择电子阅读的比例首次超过纸质阅读，达到百分之五十六；而“听书”——即通过音频收听书籍内容——的用户也在快速增长，占比已接近三成。
报告指出，青年读者的阅读时间呈现出明显的“碎片化”特点。超过六成的受访者表示，自己主要利用通勤、午休、睡前等零散时间阅读，每次阅读时间不足半小时。在阅读内容上，文学类和心理学类书籍最受欢迎，其次是历史类和经济管理类。
值得注意的是，尽管阅读人数有所增加，但“深度阅读”的比例却在下降。只有不到两成的受访者表示，在过去一年中读完过一本三百页以上的书。研究人员分析认为，短视频等娱乐方式的兴起，使得年轻人越来越难以长时间集中注意力。对此，报告建议，图书馆、书店等机构可以通过组织读书会、开设深度阅读课程等方式，引导青年养成系统阅读的习惯。

tr.en: Before clocks, how did the ancient Chinese know the time? The earliest method was watching the sun. People noticed that the length and direction of shadows change through the day, and invented the sundial: a dial marked with a scale and an upright pointer; by seeing which mark the pointer's shadow fell on, one could judge the approximate time. But it had an obvious flaw: it was useless on cloudy days and at night. To make up for this, they invented the water clock. It used water dripping steadily from a vessel: water flowed slowly from an upper pot into a lower one, in which stood a marked rod; as the water rose the rod floated up, and the time was read from its marks. Unaffected by weather or night, the water clock was used in China for over two thousand years and was still the main official timekeeper in the Ming and Qing. At night people also divided the night into five "watches" of about two hours, announced by watchmen beating drums or gongs — "striking the watches". Today's expression 三更半夜, "the third watch, the middle of the night", means late at night. These ancient ways of telling time reflect the wisdom of the ancients and have left a deep mark on the Chinese language.

items.text:
在钟表出现之前，中国古人是如何知道时间的呢？
最早的计时方法是观察太阳。古人发现，太阳照射下物体影子的长短和方向会随着时间而变化，于是发明了“日晷”。日晷由一个刻有刻度的圆盘和一根垂直的指针组成，人们通过观察指针的影子落在哪一个刻度上，就能判断出大致的时间。不过，日晷有一个明显的缺陷：阴天和夜晚无法使用。
为了弥补这一不足，古人又发明了“漏刻”。漏刻利用水从容器中匀速滴漏的原理计时：水从上面的壶慢慢流入下面的壶，下面的壶中放着一根刻有刻度的箭，随着水面上升，箭也逐渐浮起，人们根据箭上的刻度读取时间。漏刻不受天气和昼夜的限制，在中国使用了两千多年，直到明清时期仍是官方计时的主要工具。
在夜晚，古人还把一夜分为五更，每一更大约两个小时，由专人敲鼓或打锣报时，这就是“打更”。如今我们常说的“三更半夜”，指的就是深夜时分。这些古老的计时方式，不仅反映了古人的智慧，也在汉语中留下了深深的印记。

tr.en: The Mogao Caves at Dunhuang preserve a vast number of murals from the fourth to the fourteenth centuries — one of the largest and richest treasure-houses of Buddhist art in existence. These murals vividly record ancient social life, religious belief and exchange between China and other cultures. Yet they face the double threat of natural erosion and human damage. Being so old, many show flaking, hollowing and fading. At the same time, the carbon dioxide visitors breathe out and the moisture they bring speed up the murals' ageing. How to balance opening the caves to visitors with protecting the relics has long troubled their managers. In the late 1980s the Dunhuang Academy began trying digital technology. The work is called "digital capture": researchers photograph the caves section by section with high-resolution cameras, then stitch the images by computer into digital pictures almost identical to the originals. Digital protection matters in several ways: it gives restorers precise reference material, and visitors can first watch high-definition images in a digital exhibition centre and then visit the caves only briefly, greatly reducing the impact on the murals. Today the "Digital Dunhuang" project has opened images of hundreds of caves free to the whole world: anyone can open a web page and admire every detail of the caves at home, letting thousand-year-old murals "live on" in another way.

敦煌莫高窟保存着公元四世纪至十四世纪的大量壁画，是世界上现存规模最大、内容最丰富的佛教艺术宝库之一。（　）。然而，这些珍贵的壁画正面临着自然侵蚀和人为损害的双重威胁。
由于年代久远，许多壁画出现了起甲、空鼓、褪色等病害。（　），游客呼出的二氧化碳和带来的湿气，也会加速壁画的老化。如何在开放参观与保护文物之间找到平衡，一直是困扰管理者的难题。
上世纪八十年代末，敦煌研究院开始尝试用数字技术保护壁画。（　）：研究人员用高分辨率相机对洞窟进行逐块拍摄，再通过计算机拼接，最终获得与原作几乎一模一样的数字图像。
（　）。一方面，它为日后的修复工作提供了精确的参考资料；另一方面，游客可以先在数字展示中心观看洞窟的高清影像，再进入洞窟进行短时间参观，从而大大减少了对壁画的影响。
如今，“数字敦煌”项目已经将数百个洞窟的图像免费向全球公开。（　），这让千年壁画以另一种方式“活”了下来。

tr.en: The Beijing–Hangzhou Grand Canal runs from Beijing in the north to Hangzhou in the south, about 1,794 kilometres long — the earliest-dug and longest artificial canal in the world. Like the Great Wall it is regarded as one of the greatest works of ancient China, and in 2014 it was inscribed on the World Heritage List. Its history goes back over 2,500 years to the Spring and Autumn period, when Fuchai, King of Wu, wanting to march north to contend for supremacy, had a canal called the Hangou dug to link the Yangtze and the Huai — the earliest section. The canal first linked north and south on a grand scale under the Sui: in 605 Emperor Yang ordered the Tongji Canal dug, followed by the Yongji Canal and others, forming a system centred on Luoyang, reaching Zhuo Commandery in the north and Yuhang in the south. It greatly strengthened economic and cultural ties between north and south, but the immense works and excessive forced labour also burdened the people and became one cause of the Sui's rapid fall. Under the Yuan, with the capital moved to Beijing, the Luoyang-centred route was too roundabout, so the Yuan "cut the bends and straightened" it, digging new sections such as the Huitong and Tonghui canals so ships could sail straight from Hangzhou to Beijing, shortening the route by over nine hundred kilometres; today's Grand Canal basically took shape then. Through its long history its main function was "grain transport": carrying southern grain by water to the capital. Under the Ming and Qing several million dan of tribute grain went north on it every year, so it was called the dynasty's "lifeline", and many prosperous cities rose along it — Yangzhou, Suzhou, Huai'an, Linqing. After the mid-nineteenth century, with the Yellow River changing course, the rise of sea transport and the building of railways, grain transport declined and some sections even dried up. In the twenty-first century China began fully strengthening the canal's protection and use; in 2022 water ran through the whole canal for the first time in a century, and some sections reopened to shipping and tourism. Today the ancient canal, in a new guise, continues to nourish the cities and people along its banks.

items.text:
京杭大运河北起北京，南至杭州，全长约一千七百九十四公里，是世界上开凿最早、里程最长的人工运河。它与长城一样，被视为中国古代最伟大的工程之一，并于2014年被列入《世界遗产名录》。
大运河的历史可以追溯到两千五百多年前的春秋时期。当时，吴王夫差为了北上争霸，下令开凿了一条名为“邗沟”的运河，连接长江和淮河。这是大运河最早开凿的一段。
大运河真正形成贯通南北的规模，是在隋朝。公元605年，隋炀帝下令开凿通济渠，此后又陆续开凿了永济渠等河段，形成了以洛阳为中心、北达涿郡、南至余杭的运河系统。隋朝大运河的开通，极大地加强了南北之间的经济和文化联系，但由于工程浩大、征用民力过多，也加重了百姓的负担，成为隋朝迅速灭亡的原因之一。
到了元朝，由于都城迁到了北京，原来以洛阳为中心的运河绕道太远。为此，元朝对运河进行了“截弯取直”的改造，新开了会通河和通惠河等河段，使船只可以从杭州直接驶抵北京，全程缩短了九百多公里。今天我们所说的京杭大运河，基本上就是在这一时期形成的。
在漫长的历史中，大运河最主要的功能是“漕运”，即通过水路把南方的粮食运往京城。明清两代，每年经运河北上的漕粮多达数百万石，大运河因此被称为王朝的“生命线”。运河沿岸也兴起了一大批繁华的城市，如扬州、苏州、淮安、临清等。
十九世纪中期以后，随着黄河改道、海运兴起以及铁路的修建，大运河的漕运功能逐渐衰退，部分河段甚至断流。进入二十一世纪，中国开始全面加强对大运河的保护和利用。2022年，京杭大运河实现了百年来首次全线贯通补水，部分河段重新开放通航和旅游。如今，这条古老的运河正以新的面貌，继续滋养着沿岸的城市和人民。

tr.en: In recent years more and more people no longer choose a traditional nine-to-five job but become "flexible workers" — food-delivery riders, ride-hailing drivers, freelance designers, short-video creators. Statistics put China's flexible workers at over two hundred million. Its appeal lies in freedom: working hours and places are relatively flexible, and income depends largely on one's own effort. For new graduates, people caring for family and office workers wanting extra income, it clearly offers more choice. But it has obvious weak points. Without a formal labour contract with an employer, many lack pension and medical cover, and if they fall ill or meet with an accident they often can't get enough protection. Moreover, some platforms keep squeezing delivery times through their algorithms, forcing riders to risk traffic dangers to hurry — a matter of wide public concern. In response, the authorities have issued a series of policies encouraging flexible workers to join social insurance and requiring platform companies to optimise their algorithms and protect workers' legal rights. Experts think that keeping flexibility while giving workers basic security will be an important question for future labour reform.

items.text:
近年来，越来越多的人不再选择传统的“朝九晚五”工作，而是成为外卖骑手、网约车司机、自由设计师、短视频创作者等“灵活就业者”。据统计，中国灵活就业人员已超过两亿人。
灵活就业之所以吸引人，在于它的自由度高：工作时间和地点相对灵活，收入多少在很大程度上取决于个人的投入。对于刚毕业的年轻人、需要照顾家庭的人以及希望增加收入的上班族来说，这无疑提供了更多选择。
然而，灵活就业也存在明显的短板。由于没有与用人单位签订正式的劳动合同，许多灵活就业者缺乏养老、医疗等社会保障，一旦生病或遭遇意外，往往难以获得足够的保护。此外，部分平台通过算法不断压缩配送时间，使骑手不得不冒着交通风险赶时间，这也引发了社会的广泛关注。
针对这些问题，有关部门近年来出台了一系列政策，鼓励灵活就业人员参加社会保险，并要求平台企业优化算法，保障劳动者的合法权益。专家认为，如何在保持灵活性的同时为劳动者提供基本保障，将是未来劳动制度改革的重要课题。

tr.en: In summer, driving from the suburbs into the city centre, you often feel the temperature clearly rise. This phenomenon of cities being warmer than the surrounding suburbs is called the "urban heat island effect"; in some megacities the difference can exceed five degrees Celsius. The causes are several. First, the city's vast concrete and asphalt surfaces absorb heat strongly, releasing by night what they took in by day, so the city cools slowly. Second, dense high-rises block the air, so heat struggles to escape. Third, the waste heat from cars, air-conditioners and factories pushes temperatures up further. Moreover, cities have little green space or water, losing the cooling of plant transpiration and evaporation. Heat islands not only make residents feel unbearably muggy but increase air-conditioning use and energy consumption, and may even affect air quality and health. To ease them, many cities add green space, build "ventilation corridors", promote green roofs and light-coloured roofing. Research shows a fairly large city park can lower temperatures within a few hundred metres by one to two degrees.

items.text:
夏天，如果你从郊区开车进入市中心，常常会感到温度明显升高。这种城市气温高于周边郊区的现象，被称为“城市热岛效应”。在一些特大城市，市中心与郊区的温差可达五摄氏度以上。
造成热岛效应的原因是多方面的。首先，城市中大量的混凝土和沥青路面吸收热量的能力强，白天吸收的热量到了夜晚才慢慢释放，使城市降温缓慢。其次，高楼密集，阻挡了空气流通，热量难以散发。再次，汽车、空调、工厂等排放的大量废热，进一步推高了城市温度。此外，城市中绿地和水面较少，缺少了植物蒸腾和水分蒸发带来的降温作用。
热岛效应不仅让市民感到闷热难耐，还会增加空调用电量，加剧能源消耗，甚至影响空气质量和居民健康。为缓解热岛效应，许多城市采取了增加城市绿地、建设“通风廊道”、推广屋顶绿化和浅色屋面等措施。研究表明，一片面积较大的城市公园，可以使周边几百米范围内的气温下降一至两摄氏度。

tr.en: A survey of this year's graduates nationwide shows that, compared with ten years ago, their attitudes to employment are changing profoundly. When choosing a job, "personal interest and room to develop" has for the first time overtaken "pay and benefits" as the most valued factor, chosen by 43 per cent. Meanwhile more and more graduates no longer see moving to a big city as the only goal: the share choosing to work in second- or third-tier cities or their home towns has nearly doubled in ten years. They feel smaller cities cost less to live in and make work–life balance easier. Notably, "slow employment" has grown: about 12 per cent said they're in no hurry to start work after graduating but plan first to understand themselves better through study tours, internships and volunteering before choosing a career. Opinions differ: some see this as young people taking responsibility for themselves; others worry it will make them miss the best moment to enter the workplace. 一项面向全国高校应届毕业生的调查显示，与十年前相比，大学毕业生的就业观念正在发生深刻变化。
在选择工作时，“个人兴趣与发展空间”首次超过“薪资待遇”，成为毕业生最看重的因素，选择这一项的比例达到百分之四十三。与此同时，越来越多的毕业生不再把“进大城市”作为唯一目标，选择到二三线城市或家乡就业的比例比十年前增长了近一倍。他们认为，中小城市生活成本较低，工作与生活更容易达到平衡。

tr.en: The academy (shuyuan) was a distinctive educational institution of ancient China, originating in the Tang and flourishing in the Song. Unlike official schools, academies were mostly founded by private scholars, usually built in quiet mountain forests, with lecturing, book collecting and ritual offerings as their main functions. The Song was their golden age, with famous academies such as Yuelu and White Deer Grotto. They trained many talents and became centres of scholarly exchange. The great scholar Zhu Xi lectured at White Deer Grotto and drew up rules for it, stressing a method of "study widely, inquire carefully, think prudently, discriminate clearly, practise earnestly", which deeply influenced later ages. Academy education had several marked features: it emphasised students' self-study, with teachers mainly guiding; it encouraged free discussion, letting scholars of different schools debate one another; and it valued moral cultivation, putting "being a person" on a par with "reading books". At the end of the Qing, with the rise of new-style schools, the academies gradually left the historical stage. Yet the ideas they championed — independent study, free discussion — still inform educational reform today. Hunan University still counts Yuelu Academy as part of itself, so this thousand-year-old seat of learning lives on.

items.text:
书院是中国古代一种独特的教育机构，起源于唐代，兴盛于宋代。与官方设立的学校不同，书院大多由民间学者创办，一般建在环境幽静的山林之中，以讲学、藏书、祭祀为主要功能。
宋代是书院发展的黄金时期，出现了岳麓书院、白鹿洞书院等著名书院。这些书院不仅培养了大批人才，也成为学术交流的中心。著名学者朱熹曾在白鹿洞书院讲学，并为书院制定了学规，强调“博学、审问、慎思、明辨、笃行”的学习方法，对后世影响深远。
书院教育有几个显著特点：一是注重学生的自学，老师主要起引导作用；二是提倡自由讨论，不同学派的学者可以在书院中相互辩论；三是重视品德修养，把“做人”放在与“读书”同样重要的位置。
清朝末年，随着新式学堂的兴起，书院逐渐退出了历史舞台。不过，书院所倡导的自主学习、自由讨论等理念，至今仍对教育改革具有借鉴意义。如今，湖南大学仍将岳麓书院作为其组成部分，使这座千年学府延续至今。

tr.en: The twenty-four solar terms are a system of time knowledge the ancient Chinese formed by observing the sun's annual movement. It divides the year evenly into twenty-four periods of about fifteen days. In 2016 they were inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. Their names reflect changes of season, climate and farm work: "Beginning of Spring" and "Beginning of Summer" mark the start of seasons, "Minor Heat" and "Major Cold" the temperature, while "Rain Water" and "Grain Rain" concern rainfall. In farming society, farmers sowed and harvested by the terms, giving rise to many farming sayings such as "around Qingming, plant melons and beans". The terms guided farming but also deeply shaped daily life, with different customs for different terms: spring pancakes at the Beginning of Spring, outings and tomb-sweeping at Qingming, dumplings or tangyuan at the winter solstice — customs still kept in many places. With modern farming technology, the terms' role in guiding agriculture is not what it was. But they haven't lost their value: today more and more young people share solar-term knowledge and customs on social media, reminding people to follow nature and notice the changing seasons.

tr.en: The Silk Road was the ancient trade route linking China with Asia, Africa and Europe. The name was first coined in the nineteenth century by the German geographer Richthofen, because among the goods carried along it Chinese silk was the most representative. Its opening is closely tied to Zhang Qian of the Western Han. In 138 BC Emperor Wu of Han sent Zhang Qian to the Western Regions, hoping to ally with the Great Yuezhi against the Xiongnu. Twice detained by the Xiongnu on the way, he took thirteen years in all to return to Chang'an. The alliance never happened, but he brought back a wealth of information about the states of the Western Regions. In 119 BC he went again, and afterwards contacts between Han and the Western Regions grew ever more frequent. The road ran from Chang'an through the Hexi Corridor and today's Xinjiang, then west to Central and Western Asia, reaching as far as the Mediterranean coast. Along it Chinese silk, porcelain and tea went west, while western crops such as grapes and carrots, music and religion came into China. Besides the overland route there was a "Maritime Silk Road" setting out from ports on China's south-east coast, through South-East Asia to the shores of the Indian Ocean and even East Africa; in the Song and Yuan, Quanzhou became a key port, hailed as "the greatest port in the East". After the fifteenth century, with new sea routes and changes in Central Asia, the overland road declined. In 2014 "Silk Roads: the Routes Network of Chang'an-Tianshan Corridor" was inscribed on the World Heritage List. Today the Silk Road has become a symbol of cultural exchange between East and West.

丝绸之路是古代连接中国与亚洲、非洲、欧洲的商业贸易路线。“丝绸之路”这一名称，是十九世纪德国地理学家李希霍芬首先提出的，因为在这条路上运输的商品中，以中国的丝绸最具代表性。
丝绸之路的开辟，与西汉时期的张骞密切相关。公元前138年，汉武帝派张骞出使西域，希望联合大月氏共同对付匈奴。张骞在途中两次被匈奴扣留，前后历经十三年才回到长安。虽然联合大月氏的目的没有实现，但张骞带回了大量关于西域各国的信息。公元前119年，张骞第二次出使西域。此后，汉朝与西域各国的往来日益频繁。
丝绸之路东起长安，经过河西走廊，穿越今天的新疆，再向西延伸到中亚、西亚，最远可达地中海沿岸。通过这条道路，中国的丝绸、瓷器、茶叶等被运往西方，而西方的葡萄、胡萝卜等作物以及音乐、宗教也传入了中国。
除了陆上丝绸之路，还有一条“海上丝绸之路”。它从中国东南沿海的港口出发，经过东南亚，到达印度洋沿岸乃至东非。宋元时期，泉州成为海上丝绸之路的重要港口，被誉为“东方第一大港”。
十五世纪以后，随着海上航线的开辟和中亚局势的变化，陆上丝绸之路逐渐衰落。2014年，“丝绸之路：长安—天山廊道的路网”被列入《世界遗产名录》。今天，丝绸之路已经成为东西方文化交流的象征。

tr.en: "Pre-made dishes" are dishes made from farm produce, processed and packaged in advance, which consumers need only heat or cook briefly to eat. In recent years the market has grown rapidly, estimated at over five hundred billion yuan. Their rise is closely tied to modern lifestyles: for busy office workers with no time to cook they save time and effort; for restaurants they cut labour costs and keep flavours consistent. In the takeaway business especially, they have become an important choice for many sellers. But they have also caused controversy. Some diners discovered that the "freshly stir-fried" dish they ordered was in fact a reheated pre-made one and felt cheated. Moreover, to extend shelf life some contain a lot of salt and preservatives, which may be bad for health if eaten long-term. Insiders say that for the industry to develop healthily it needs unified standards to regulate production, and consumers' right to know must be protected: restaurants that use pre-made dishes should tell customers clearly. Only then can they win consumers' trust.

items.text:
所谓“预制菜”，是指以农产品为原料，经过预先加工、包装，消费者只需简单加热或烹调即可食用的菜品。近年来，预制菜市场规模迅速扩大，据估计已超过五千亿元。
预制菜的兴起与现代人的生活方式密切相关。对于工作繁忙、没有时间做饭的上班族来说，预制菜省时省力；对于餐饮企业而言，使用预制菜可以降低人工成本，保证菜品口味的稳定。尤其是在外卖行业，预制菜已经成为许多商家的重要选择。
然而，预制菜也引发了不少争议。一些消费者在餐厅点菜时，发现自己吃到的“现炒”菜品其实是加热后的预制菜，感到被欺骗。此外，部分预制菜为了延长保质期，添加了较多的盐和防腐剂，长期食用可能对健康不利。
业内人士认为，预制菜行业要健康发展，一方面要制定统一的行业标准，规范生产过程；另一方面应保障消费者的知情权，餐厅如果使用预制菜，应当明确告知顾客。只有这样，才能赢得消费者的信任。

tr.en: We spend about a third of our lives asleep. For a long time people thought sleep's main purpose was to rest the body, but recent research reveals it is just as vital to the brain. Scientists have found that during sleep the spaces between brain cells widen, letting fluid flow more freely and flush out the metabolic waste built up during the day — a process far less efficient when awake. Some scientists vividly call it "the brain's night cleaner". Besides clearing waste, sleep plays an important part in forming memories. New knowledge learnt in the day is at first only stored temporarily in one region of the brain; during sleep, especially deep sleep, this information is "replayed" and moved to regions responsible for long-term memory, consolidating it. That also explains why cramming late before an exam often works worse than getting enough sleep. Researchers warn that long-term lack of sleep not only lowers concentration and unsettles mood but may raise the risk of many diseases. For adults, seven to nine hours a night is ideal.

items.text:
人的一生中大约有三分之一的时间是在睡眠中度过的。长期以来，人们一直认为睡眠的主要作用是让身体休息。然而，近年来的研究揭示，睡眠对大脑来说同样至关重要。
科学家发现，人在睡眠时，大脑细胞之间的空隙会扩大，脑内的液体能够更加顺畅地流动，把白天积累下来的代谢废物冲洗出去。这一过程在清醒状态下效率要低得多。有科学家形象地把它比作“大脑的夜间清洁工”。
除了清除废物，睡眠还在记忆形成中扮演着重要角色。白天学习的新知识，最初只是暂时储存在大脑的某个区域。在睡眠过程中，尤其是在深度睡眠阶段，这些信息会被“重放”，并转移到负责长期记忆的区域，从而得到巩固。这也解释了为什么考试前熬夜复习的效果往往不如保证充足的睡眠。
研究人员提醒，长期睡眠不足不仅会导致注意力下降、情绪不稳，还可能增加患多种疾病的风险。对于成年人来说，每晚保证七到九个小时的睡眠是比较理想的。

tr.en: The recently released "Survey on Urban Residents' Exercise" shows that of ten thousand city residents surveyed, "regular exercisers" — those exercising at least three times a week for over thirty minutes — made up 37 per cent, eight points more than five years ago. Running, brisk walking and cycling are the most popular, together over half. Notably, new sports such as ultimate frisbee, paddleboarding and hiking have taken off among young people, with participation growing over 30 per cent a year. Compared with traditional sports they stress the social side: many young people say they take part not only to keep fit but to meet like-minded friends. The survey also found the main obstacles to exercise are, in order, "no time", "no place" and "no partner"; "no place" was chosen most by middle-aged and older people. Experts suggest cities make full use of parks, riverbanks and space under bridges to build more facilities for exercising nearby, creating "fifteen-minute fitness circles".

items.text:
近日发布的《城市居民运动健身状况调查》显示，在被调查的一万名城市居民中，每周至少锻炼三次、每次三十分钟以上的“经常锻炼者”占比达到百分之三十七，比五年前提高了八个百分点。
在运动项目的选择上，跑步、健步走和骑自行车最受欢迎，三项合计占比超过一半。值得注意的是，近年来飞盘、桨板、徒步等新兴运动在年轻人中迅速走红，参与人数年均增长超过百分之三十。与传统运动相比，这些新兴运动更强调社交属性。很多年轻人表示，参加这些运动不仅是为了锻炼身体，更是为了认识志同道合的朋友。
调查还发现，影响居民参加锻炼的主要因素依次是“没有时间”“缺乏场地”和“缺少同伴”。其中，选择“缺乏场地”的比例在中老年群体中最高。专家建议，城市在规划时应充分利用公园、河道、桥下空间等，建设更多方便居民就近锻炼的健身设施，打造“十五分钟健身圈”。

tr.en: Printing is one of ancient China's Four Great Inventions. The first form was woodblock printing: a whole page of text was carved in reverse on a wooden block, inked and covered with paper to print one page. It was far faster than copying by hand but had obvious drawbacks: every page needed its own block, costing time and effort; once a book was printed the blocks were often useless; and one wrongly carved character could ruin a whole block. In the Northern Song a craftsman named Bi Sheng invented movable type. He made separate characters from clay, one stamp per character, and hardened them in fire to form "movable type". To print, the needed characters were set in order on an iron plate and fixed; afterwards they were taken apart and could be used again. Movable type greatly raised efficiency and saved materials. But because Chinese has so many characters, making and picking type was a great deal of work, so for a long time woodblock and movable-type printing coexisted in China. Movable type later spread to Korea, Japan and elsewhere, with a far-reaching effect on the spread of culture worldwide.

items.text:
印刷术是中国古代的四大发明之一。最早出现的是雕版印刷：人们把整页文字反刻在一块木板上，刷上墨，再铺上纸，就能印出一页书。雕版印刷比手抄快得多，但也有明显的缺点：每印一页书都要刻一块版，费时费力；印完一本书后，这些木板往往就没有用了；如果刻错一个字，整块木板都可能作废。
北宋时期，一位名叫毕昇的工匠发明了活字印刷术。他用胶泥制成一个个单独的字，每个字一个印，然后用火烧硬，成为“活字”。印书时，把需要的活字按顺序排在铁板上，固定好以后就可以印刷；印完以后，再把活字拆下来，下次还能继续使用。
活字印刷大大提高了印刷效率，也节省了材料。不过，由于汉字数量众多，制作和挑选活字的工作量很大，因此在很长一段时间里，雕版印刷和活字印刷在中国是并存的。后来，活字印刷术传到了朝鲜、日本等地，对世界文化的传播产生了深远的影响。

tr.en: The Tea Horse Road is an ancient trade route in south-west China, running mainly between Yunnan, Sichuan and Tibet. Its history goes back to the Tang and Song. Because it mainly carried tea and horses it is called the "Tea Horse Road". It arose from local conditions: the Tibetan plateau is cold, people there live mainly on meat and dairy and need tea to aid digestion, while inland China needed Tibet's fine horses. So the two sides began trading tea for horses. The route is steep and dangerous, with many stretches along cliffs; in places it is only wide enough for one horse. The men who carried the goods were called "mabang" (horse caravans); driving mules and horses, they would be on the road for months, often at risk of their lives. The road was not only a trade route: many important towns and markets grew up along it, promoting cultural exchange between different peoples. Today it has long lost its transport function, but many remains along it survive, an important window onto this history.

茶马古道是中国西南地区一条古老的商贸通道，主要分布在云南、四川和西藏之间。（　）。由于这条路以运输茶叶和马匹为主，所以被称为“茶马古道”。
茶马古道的形成与当地的自然条件密切相关。西藏高原气候寒冷，人们以肉类和奶制品为主食，需要喝茶来帮助消化；（　）。于是，双方开始了以茶换马的贸易。
茶马古道沿途地势险峻，很多路段在悬崖峭壁上，（　）。运送货物的人被称为“马帮”，他们赶着骡马，一走就是几个月，常常要冒着生命危险。
（　），沿途还形成了许多重要的城镇和集市，促进了不同民族之间的文化交流。（　），但古道沿线的许多遗迹被保存了下来，成为人们了解这段历史的重要窗口。

tr.en: Zheng He was a famous navigator of the Ming dynasty. From 1405 to 1433, on the orders of the Yongle Emperor Zhu Di, he led a huge fleet on seven voyages, known as "Zheng He's voyages to the Western Oceans" — meaning the seas west of today's South China Sea and their coasts. The fleet was of unprecedented size: on the first voyage it had over two hundred ships and more than twenty-seven thousand people; the largest ships, the "treasure ships", were about 130 metres long. Besides sailors and soldiers it carried doctors, interpreters, craftsmen and others. Setting out from Liujiagang in Taicang, Jiangsu, it passed through South-East and South Asia, reaching as far as Western Asia and the east coast of Africa, visiting over thirty countries and regions. It took Chinese silk, porcelain and tea to trade for spices, jewels, medicinal herbs and other local products, and envoys from some countries came back with it to China, establishing friendly relations with the Ming. Zheng He's voyages came over eighty years before Columbus reached the Americas and over ninety before Vasco da Gama reached India, holding an important place in the history of navigation. Unlike the colonial expansion of later European navigators, his fleet aimed mainly at peaceful contact and trade and occupied no one's land. In 1433 Zheng He died on the way home from the seventh voyage. Afterwards the Ming enforced a strict maritime ban and large-scale ocean voyages stopped. To commemorate him, China made 11 July — the day of his first voyage — "China Maritime Day".

items.text:
郑和是明朝著名的航海家。1405年至1433年，他奉明成祖朱棣之命，先后七次率领庞大的船队远航，史称“郑和下西洋”。这里的“西洋”，指的是今天南海以西的海洋及沿岸地区。
郑和的船队规模空前。第一次出航时，船队共有二百多艘船，随行人员两万七千多人，其中最大的船被称为“宝船”，长约一百三十多米。船队中除了水手和士兵，还有医生、翻译、工匠等各种人员。
郑和的船队从江苏太仓刘家港出发，经过东南亚、南亚，最远到达了西亚和非洲东海岸，一共访问了三十多个国家和地区。船队带去了中国的丝绸、瓷器、茶叶等物品，与各地交换香料、珠宝、药材等特产。一些国家的使者也随船队来到中国，与明朝建立了友好往来。
郑和下西洋比哥伦布发现美洲早了八十多年，比达·伽马到达印度早了九十多年，在世界航海史上具有重要地位。与后来欧洲航海家的殖民扩张不同，郑和的船队主要以和平交往和贸易为目的，没有占领他国的土地。
1433年，郑和在第七次远航的返航途中去世。此后，明朝实行了严格的海禁政策，大规模的远洋航行停止了。为了纪念郑和，中国将每年的7月11日——郑和首次下西洋的日子——定为“中国航海日”。

tr.en: In recent years artificial intelligence has developed at great speed; from automatic writing and smart customer service to driverless cars, it is taking over human work in more and more fields. This has raised a common worry: will AI take our jobs? Historically, every major technological revolution has made some occupations disappear while creating new ones. The industrial revolution put many craftsmen out of work but brought factory workers and engineers; the spread of the internet hit some traditional industries but gave rise to online shop owners, programmers and livestreamers. AI will very likely follow the same pattern. Research shows the jobs AI most easily replaces are repetitive ones with clear rules — data entry, simple customer service — while jobs needing creativity, emotional exchange and complex judgement, such as teachers, counsellors and researchers, are relatively hard to replace. Experts point out that, facing AI's challenge, what matters most for individuals is keeping the ability to learn and constantly updating knowledge and skills, while governments and companies should strengthen job training to help workers make the transition. Rather than worrying about being replaced by machines, learn to work with them.

items.text:
近年来，人工智能技术飞速发展，从自动写作、智能客服到无人驾驶，它正在越来越多的领域代替人类完成工作。这引发了人们普遍的担忧：人工智能会不会抢走我们的饭碗？
从历史上看，每一次重大的技术革命都会让一些职业消失，同时又创造出新的职业。工业革命让大量手工业者失去了工作，却也带来了工厂工人、工程师等新职业；互联网的普及让一些传统行业受到冲击，却催生了网店店主、程序员、网络主播等新岗位。人工智能很可能也会遵循这一规律。
研究表明，最容易被人工智能代替的，是那些重复性强、规则明确的工作，如数据录入、简单的客户服务等；而需要创造力、情感交流和复杂判断的工作，如教师、心理咨询师、研究人员等，则相对不容易被代替。
专家指出，面对人工智能带来的挑战，个人最重要的是保持学习的能力，不断更新自己的知识和技能；政府和企业则应当加强职业培训，帮助劳动者顺利完成转型。与其担心被机器代替，不如学会与机器合作。

tr.en: Drought is one of the main natural disasters threatening farming. To relieve it, people invented "artificial rain". It doesn't "make" rain out of nothing but acts on clouds that already exist so they rain more easily. Clouds consist of masses of tiny water droplets and ice crystals, so small that they float in the air and can hardly fall by themselves. Artificial rain uses aircraft, rockets and the like to deliver catalysts such as dry ice into the clouds; these help small droplets condense into larger drops or crystals, which, once too heavy for the air to hold, fall as rain. It must be said that artificial rain needs certain conditions: without suitable clouds, or with too little moisture in them, no catalyst will bring rain. So it can only "add flowers to brocade", improving what is there, not "create something from nothing". Besides relieving drought, weather-modification technology is used to prevent hail and secure the weather for major events. But some scientists warn that human interference with the weather may affect local ecology, and its long-term consequences need further study.

items.text:
干旱是威胁农业生产的主要自然灾害之一。为了缓解旱情，人们发明了“人工降雨”技术。
人工降雨并不是凭空“造”出雨来，而是对已经存在的云施加影响，使它更容易下雨。云是由大量的小水滴和小冰晶组成的，这些水滴和冰晶非常小，在空中飘浮着，很难自己落到地面。人工降雨的方法，就是用飞机、火箭等把干冰等催化剂送入云中。这些催化剂能促使小水滴凝结成较大的水滴或冰晶，当它们重到空气托不住时，就会落下来形成降雨。
需要指出的是，人工降雨必须具备一定的条件。如果天空中没有合适的云，或者云中的水汽不足，即使施放了催化剂，也无法下雨。因此，人工降雨只能“锦上添花”，而不能“无中生有”。
除了缓解干旱，人工影响天气的技术还被用于防止冰雹、为重大活动保障天气等。不过，也有科学家提醒，人类对天气的干预可能会对局部地区的生态环境产生影响，其长期后果还有待进一步研究。

tr.en: According to a travel platform's "Annual Tourism Spending Report", domestic trips and tourism revenue both hit record highs last year. Spontaneous short trips and outings near home made up over sixty per cent of all trips, the main way people travelled. The report shows the make-up of tourist spenders is changing: those born in the 1990s and 2000s are now the main force, over half the total. Unlike the previous generation, keen on "checking in" at famous sights, the young value experiences — learning a local traditional craft, going to a music festival, or staying a few days in an old town to live like the locals. "Reverse tourism" and "off-peak travel" are increasingly popular: more and more travellers avoid holiday peaks and head for less popular cities and sights for a more comfortable trip, bringing opportunities to small towns that once saw few visitors. The report also notes problems: poor service at some sights, opaque prices, crowding at holidays. It suggests sights and local governments raise service standards and tighten market supervision so tourists can enjoy themselves with peace of mind.

根据某旅游平台发布的《年度旅游消费报告》，过去一年，国内旅游人次和旅游收入均创下历史新高。其中，“说走就走”的短途游和周边游占全部出游次数的六成以上，成为最主要的出游方式。
报告显示，旅游消费的群体结构正在发生变化。“90后”和“00后”已成为旅游消费的主力军，占比超过一半。与上一代人热衷于“打卡”著名景点不同，年轻人更看重旅途中的体验，比如学习一门当地的传统技艺、参加一场音乐节，或者在古镇住上几天，体验当地人的生活。
在出游方式上，“反向旅游”“错峰出游”越来越流行。越来越多的游客选择避开节假日高峰，前往热度较低的城市或景区，以获得更舒适的旅行体验。这也给一些过去游客较少的小城带来了发展机遇。
报告同时指出，旅游市场仍存在一些问题，如部分景区服务质量不高、价格不透明、节假日拥挤等。报告建议，景区和地方政府应提升服务水平，加强市场监管，让游客玩得开心、放心。

tr.en: Peking opera is one of China's national treasures, over two hundred years old. In performance, the patterns and colours painted on actors' faces are called "facial makeup" (lianpu). It is decorative, but more importantly it helps the audience grasp a character's personality and identity at once. The colours have set meanings: generally red stands for loyalty and courage, as with Guan Yu; black for integrity and selflessness, as with Bao Zheng; white often for treachery and suspicion, as with Cao Cao; blue for fierceness and toughness. Seeing an actor's makeup, the audience can roughly tell whether the character is good or bad and what kind of person they are — an expression of the "suggestive" (xieyi) art of traditional Chinese theatre. Besides colour, the patterns too are carefully devised: eyebrows, eyes and noses are painted differently for different roles, and some mythical figures have gold or silver painted on to show their special status. Today lianpu has become an important symbol of Chinese culture, widely used in designs for clothes, toys and crafts.

items.text:
京剧是中国的国粹之一，已有两百多年的历史。在京剧表演中，演员脸上画的各种图案和颜色被称为“脸谱”。脸谱不仅具有装饰作用，更重要的是，它能帮助观众迅速了解人物的性格和身份。
脸谱的颜色有着特定的含义。一般来说，红色代表忠诚、勇敢，如关羽；黑色代表正直、无私，如包拯；白色则常常代表奸诈、多疑，如曹操；蓝色表示勇猛、刚强。观众一看到演员的脸谱，就能大致判断出这个角色是好人还是坏人，性格是怎样的。这种表现方式，体现了中国传统戏曲“写意”的艺术特点。
除了颜色，脸谱的图案也大有讲究。不同角色的眉毛、眼睛、鼻子的画法各不相同，一些神话人物的脸谱上还会画上金色或银色，以显示其特殊身份。
如今，京剧脸谱已经成为中国文化的一个重要标志，被广泛应用于服装、玩具、工艺品等设计中。

tr.en: The giant panda is a rare animal found only in China, hailed as a "national treasure". Today wild pandas live mainly in the mountains of south-west China. But because of human activity their habitat was once broken into many isolated "islands", making contact between populations hard and hampering breeding. To solve this, in 2021 China formally set up Giant Panda National Park, joining many reserves across Sichuan, Shaanxi and Gansu into one whole. This removed the boundaries between the old reserves, letting pandas roam over a far larger area. Within the park human activity is strictly limited. Some residents of the core zones moved to new homes, and local governments help them develop eco-tourism, specialty farming and other industries. This protects the pandas' home and raises local incomes — a win-win for conservation and development. After years of protection, the number of wild pandas has risen from just over 1,100 in the 1980s to nearly 1,900 today. Although the threat to them has eased, protecting them is still a long road.

tr.en: Dujiangyan, in Chengdu, Sichuan, is the oldest — and the only surviving and still working — large water-control project in the world characterised by diverting water without a dam. Built around 256 BC under the direction of Li Bing, governor of the Qin state's Shu Commandery, and his son, it is over 2,200 years old. Before it was built, the Min River often flooded, bringing severe floods to the Chengdu Plain, while in the dry season there were often droughts. To solve this, Li Bing led the local people for years to complete the great work. It has three main parts: the Fish Mouth, the Flying Sand Weir and the Bottle-Neck Channel. The Fish Mouth, built mid-river and shaped like a fish's mouth, splits the Min into an inner and an outer river: the inner for irrigation, the outer for flood discharge. The Flying Sand Weir drains off surplus water and silt. The Bottle-Neck Channel is the "throat" controlling how much water enters the inner river, named for its bottle-mouth shape. Working together, the three parts ingeniously divide the water, discharge the sand and draw off water. After it was built, the Chengdu Plain no longer feared flood or drought and became the fertile "Land of Abundance". In 2000 Dujiangyan and Mount Qingcheng were inscribed together on the World Heritage List. To this day it irrigates over ten million mu of farmland and plays an important part in local farming and life.

items.text:
都江堰位于四川省成都市，是世界上年代最久、唯一留存、仍在使用的以无坝引水为特征的大型水利工程。它建于公元前256年左右，由秦国蜀郡太守李冰父子主持修建，至今已有两千两百多年的历史。
都江堰修建以前，岷江经常泛滥，给成都平原带来严重的水灾；而到了枯水季节，又常常出现旱灾。为了解决这一问题，李冰带领当地百姓，经过多年努力，建成了这项伟大的工程。
都江堰主要由三个部分组成：鱼嘴、飞沙堰和宝瓶口。鱼嘴建在江心，形状像鱼的嘴巴，它把岷江分为内江和外江，内江用于灌溉，外江用于排洪。飞沙堰的作用是排出多余的江水和泥沙。宝瓶口则是控制进入内江水量的“咽喉”，因为形状像瓶口而得名。三个部分相互配合，巧妙地实现了分水、排沙和引水的功能。
都江堰建成以后，成都平原从此不再害怕水旱灾害，成为物产丰富的“天府之国”。2000年，都江堰与青城山一起被列入《世界遗产名录》。直到今天，都江堰仍然灌溉着一千多万亩农田，为当地的农业生产和人民生活发挥着重要作用。
